name: Cindergrain Godmask Devotional Coat
description:
A floor-length devotional coat worn by practitioners of the Meridian Convergence faith — a syncretic 2200 belief system blending West African Ifá, Japanese Shinto animism, and digital transcendence theology. The base is undyed heavy linen-analog in warm bone-white, hand-block-printed with interlocking Nsibidi script and circuit-path mandalas in iron-gall ink that darkens with age. Each coat is made by the wearer's shrine community, and the printing ceremony is itself a ritual act.

The back panel bears an embroidered 'godmask' — a geometric face assembled from both traditional masquerade forms and BCI port diagrams, symbolizing the divine as both ancient and networked. Sleeves have wide bell cuts to accommodate horn or wing geneware.
functionality: Wide bell sleeves accommodate wing and horn geneware; loose back cut fits spinal rigs; iron-gall printing becomes more distinctive with age and wear, marking long-term devotion.
what_it_says: You belong to something older and stranger than any corponation — and you are not afraid to say so in public.
worn_by: spiritual runners who tithe to the network
price_range: Not sold — gifted by community upon initiation
story_hooks: A Tier 5 corponation exec has been secretly attending Convergence shrines — someone spotted the coat under a concealment wrap and wants to know why.
A shrine's block-printing plates were stolen; without them, the next generation of coats cannot be properly consecrated, and the community is fracturing over what to do.
The BCI port diagrams embroidered into the godmask are real — traced from a proprietary neural architecture that should not be public knowledge.
related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions ChemoShield BX-2 Dermal Toxin Barrier Implant

physical_description.visual_profile: A flowing, ceremonial floor-length coat with an ethereal presence. The silhouette is deliberately voluminous yet structured, suggesting both spiritual reverence and practical accommodation for augmented bodies. The bell sleeves create dramatic movement; the back panel commands visual attention with its embedded godmask embroidery. Overall impression is sacred vestment meets cutting-edge body modification culture.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and accommodating through the torso and limbs, with intentional oversizing at the sleeves to clear horn, wing, or limb augmentations. The coat drapes naturally from the shoulders, designed for ritual movement and non-restrictive wear during extended ceremonies.
physical_description.primary_material: Undyed heavy linen-analog (synthetic linen composite with natural fiber simulant properties) in warm bone-white, hand-treated for durability and age-darkening potential.
physical_description.texture: Tactile and deliberately rustic—the linen-analog has a slightly nubbed weave. Hand-block printed areas show subtle ink saturation variations. The embroidered godmask panel features raised threadwork with mixed fiber texture (including likely metallic threads for circuit-path detail). Overall texture reads as hand-crafted, never industrially slick.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: warm off-white/bone linen base. Secondary: iron-gall ink prints in deep warm brown-black that will age to richer charcoal tones. Embroidery likely incorporates copper, silver, or holographic thread highlights within the godmask for sacred/technological duality. Some shrines may add ritual staining (intentional dye marks) over years of use.
physical_description.closures: No visible closures—the coat is worn open and draped, held in place by its own weight and the wearer's intention. This is ceremonial, not functional closure design.
distinctive_features: Hand-block-printed Nsibidi script (West African writing system) interlocking with circuit-path mandalas across the full body
Large embroidered godmask on back panel: geometric face combining traditional masquerade forms with BCI port/neural interface diagrams
Bell sleeves sized to clear horn geneware, wing implants, or cybernetic limbs
Iron-gall ink darkening signature—each coat's aging is visible, marking the wearer's spiritual journey
Entirely shrine-made: no mass production markers, unique hand variations in each garment
Ritual printing ceremony integral to creation—the coat is consecrated during manufacture
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 devotional wear. While hand-made with care, it signals community belonging rather than wealth. The materials are humble but intentional; the labor is spiritual rather than premium.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn exclusively by practitioners of the Meridian Convergence faith—a syncretic belief system. Signals deep spiritual commitment, openness to body augmentation as sacred practice, and alignment with the global neo-animism movements of 2226. Wearing this marks the wearer as part of an intentional community, not a corpo or street wanderer.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when first shrine-gifted, but expected to age gracefully. Over years, the iron-gall ink darkens from warm brown to deep charcoal, creating an unplanned archive of the wearer's spiritual practice. Likely accumulates ritual marks, minor stains, and wear at the hem—all honored as evidence of devotional use. Never patched or 'fixed'—damage becomes part of the sacred record.

image_prompt: A floor-length devotional coat displayed on a dark mannequin or worn by a model with visible augmentation (horn geneware or cybernetic limbs). The coat is undyed bone-white heavy linen, draped open. The back is turned toward camera, showcasing an intricate embroidered godmask—a geometric face merging West African masquerade forms with neural BCI port diagrams in copper and silver thread. The body is hand-block-printed with dark iron-gall ink Nsibidi script interlocking with circuit-path mandalas. Bell sleeves hang dramatically. Moody museum-like lighting from above, cool shadows emphasizing the embroidery. Dark urban shrine interior or minimalist gallery backdrop. The coat reads as sacred and ancient yet unmistakably 2226. Slight visible aging/darkening of the ink print. Cinematic, respectful framing. --ar 2:3 --v 6
